news.headline: Palo Alto Networks Beats Q3 Estimates With $3B Revenue, Raises Q4 Guidance; Stock Swings
news.body: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) reported fiscal Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.85 versus the $0.80 consensus, on revenue of $3.00 billion that grew 31% year-over-year and topped the $2.94 billion estimate. Next Generation Security ARR surged 60% year-over-year to $8.13 billion, and next-generation firewall bookings posted their best quarter in a decade. The company issued above-consensus Q4 revenue guidance of $3.35–$3.36 billion versus the $3.28 billion estimate, and raised full-year revenue guidance to $11.42–$11.43 billion. Shares whipsawed in after-hours trade, rising as much as 12% before fading to near flat, as investors weighed a GAAP net loss of $177 million against the otherwise strong operational print.

news.headline: Marvell Tech Surges ~30% After Nvidia CEO Huang Calls It 'Next Trillion-Dollar Company'
news.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a surprise appearance at Marvell Technology CEO Matt Murphy's Computex 2026 keynote in Taipei on June 2, publicly declaring Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company' and highlighting its networking and connectivity chips as essential to AI data centers. Shares soared roughly 25–32% on the session, adding billions in market cap against a pre-rally figure of around $250 billion. The endorsement was amplified by Nvidia's existing $2 billion investment in Marvell and a newly announced strategic partnership. The move sparked a broad AI infrastructure rally, lifting Broadcom, Qualcomm, and Lam Research more than 5% each.

news.headline: Alphabet Launches $80B Stock Sale to Fund AI Buildout; Shares Drop ~4%
news.body: Alphabet announced equity offerings totaling $80 billion on June 1, structured as $30 billion in concurrent underwritten public offerings and a $40 billion at-the-market program beginning Q3 2026, to fund AI compute infrastructure expansion. Berkshire Hathaway agreed to a $10 billion private placement in Class A and Class C stock, lifting its total Alphabet stake to approximately $32 billion. The scale of the dilutive raise — a dramatic reversal from Alphabet's historic buyback posture — sent shares down roughly 4%, weighing on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq. Wall Street noted the move signals AI capex demand has materially outpaced available internal capacity.

news.headline: Microchip Technology Jumps ~12% as Data Center Unit Eyes 65% Revenue Growth in 2026
news.body: Microchip Technology (MCHP) shares popped roughly 12% on June 2 after the company disclosed that its Data Center Solutions Business Unit generated $302.7 million in revenue in 2025 and now expects approximately $500 million — roughly 65% growth — by end of calendar 2026. The data center unit's revenue was already up 62.9% year-over-year in the March 2026 quarter, fueled by storage controllers, PCIe/CXL memory controllers, and newly launched XpressConnect PCIe 6.0 products for AI data centers. Management also announced selective product price increases to protect margins against broad-based input cost pressures, while UBS reiterated a Buy rating with a $130 price target. The disclosure marks the first time Microchip has broken out the segment separately, adding transparency that investors rewarded immediately.

news.headline: HPE Surges ~25% on AI-Fueled Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance
news.body: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reported fiscal Q2 results that topped analyst estimates on both earnings and revenue, and raised its full-year guidance citing surging demand for AI server infrastructure on June 2. Shares jumped approximately 25% on the session, one of the stock's largest single-day moves on record. The result reinforces the broadening AI hardware spending cycle beyond pure-play chipmakers into server OEMs. HPE's guidance upgrade also lifted peer Dell Technologies and contributed to the S&P 500 closing above 7,600 for the first time.

news.headline: Nikkei 225 Hits Fresh All-Time High Above 68,000 as AI Rally Drives Wed. Open
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 extended gains on Wednesday, June 3, rising as much as 2.94% intraday and surpassing 68,100 — a new record high — with the Topix adding 2.14%, as investors looked past U.S.-Iran negotiation uncertainty to focus on AI-driven semiconductor optimism. The record comes after SoftBank surged 14%+ on June 1 to overtake Toyota as Japan's most valuable company, following its pledge of €75 billion in AI infrastructure investment in France. Markets are also pricing in an 86.5% probability of a Bank of Japan rate hike to 1.00% at the June 15–16 meeting, adding a macro policy overhang. The rally is broad-based across AI hardware names, with Topix posting successive record closes.

news.headline: TSMC Surges on Computex: Nvidia Expands Taiwan Investment, 3nm Price Hike Flagged
news.body: Taiwan's TAIEX closed at a record 45,557.31 on June 2, driven by TSMC hitting a fresh 52-week high after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced a dramatic expansion of annual investment in Taiwan at Computex 2026, directly boosting fab utilization outlook for TSMC as Nvidia's primary AI chip manufacturer. Supply chain sources separately indicated TSMC plans to raise 3nm process pricing by up to 15% in H2 2026, with accelerating adoption by Nvidia, AMD, Google, and AWS cited as the driver. Taiwan's total market cap surpassed $5 trillion for the first time at end-May 2026, reinforcing the TWSE's position as the world's fifth-largest exchange. With ~81% of TWSE cap in tech, the index remains a direct proxy for global AI capex.

news.headline: BOJ June Rate Hike Odds Hit 86.5%; Himino Reaffirms Tightening Path Amid Iran Inflation
news.body: Market-implied probability of a Bank of Japan rate hike to 1.00% at the June 15–16 meeting reached 86.5% as of June 2, following hawkish communications from Deputy Governor Himino who reaffirmed the BoJ's commitment to further hikes while noting monitoring of Middle East energy risks. The BoJ's April 28 meeting produced a 6-3 split vote to hold at 0.75%, with three dissenters pushing for an immediate hike; core inflation rose to 2.8% on energy pass-through effects from the Iran conflict. A Reuters poll showed 65% of economists expect a June hike. A tighter BoJ at 1.00% would carry yen carry-trade unwind implications for regional equity risk appetite, particularly for Nikkei exporters and levered Asian positions.

news.headline: NIO Deliveries Surge 62% YoY in May; EV Stocks Jump on HK Exchange
news.body: NIO reported 37,705 vehicle deliveries in May 2026, a 62.3% year-on-year and 28.4% month-on-month jump, driven by new ONVO L80 SUV and ES8 demand, sending Hong Kong-listed shares up ~6.7% on June 1. XPeng (HK: 9868) also rose ~6–8% in HK trade after reporting 32,158 May deliveries, up 4% sequentially; Hang Seng technology names broadly firmed. The combined three-brand NIO/XPeng/Li Auto total of 103,213 deliveries, up 6% YoY, outperformed the broader China new car market, which fell ~7% in Q1 2026. Investors read the data as evidence of continued share gains by premium EV brands within a soft overall Chinese auto market.

news.headline: Gold Holds Below $4,500 as Strong JOLTS Data Cements Fed Rate-Hike Bets
news.body: Gold traded below $4,500/oz on Wednesday after US April job openings surged to their highest level in nearly two years, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve may raise rates before year-end. Markets are now fully pricing out cuts for 2026, with some traders pricing in at least one 25bp hike as inflation—driven largely by the Middle East conflict—continues to accelerate. The metal remains caught between safe-haven demand from the Hormuz crisis and headwinds from a hawkish policy repricing. Investors now await Friday's nonfarm payrolls for confirmation of the labour-market signal.

news.headline: WTI Steady Near $91–$92 After Monday's 5.5% Surge on Iran Hormuz Deadlock
news.body: WTI crude futures held around $91–$92/bbl Tuesday and Wednesday after a 5.5% single-session spike Monday, triggered by Iranian media reports that Tehran had suspended communications with Washington following Israeli attacks in Lebanon. Prices pulled back modestly after President Trump insisted talks were ongoing and suggested a Strait of Hormuz MOU could come within a week, but conflicting signals from Trump and Netanyahu on Lebanon kept volatility elevated. The Strait, closed since late February, has removed ~20% of global oil supply; EIA expects global inventories to draw by 8.5 mb/d in Q2 2026. Oil implied volatility has averaged 78% since the conflict began.

news.headline: Copper Hits All-Time High of $6.65/lb on Chile's 23-Year Output Low and Tariff Shift
news.body: COMEX copper surged to an all-time record of $6.65/lb on Tuesday, gaining 14.75% over the past four weeks and 37.52% over the past year. Chile, the world's largest copper producer, reported its weakest April output in 23 years, while Codelco's new chairman signalled a pivot to profitability over volume. President Trump also signed a proclamation adjusting metals tariffs on national-security grounds, widening the US copper premium and potentially drawing fresh inflows into US ports. AI data-centre buildout and energy-transition demand continue to anchor the bullish demand thesis against a structurally constrained supply backdrop.

news.headline: TTF Gas Rebounds 6.7% on Iran's Bab el-Mandeb Threat; Europe Storage at 38%
news.body: European TTF natural gas futures surged 6.7% Monday to approach €49/MWh after Iran threatened to extend its Hormuz blockade to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a second critical chokepoint, in retaliation for Israeli operations in Lebanon. The Strait of Hormuz closure has already cut roughly one-fifth of global LNG flows for over three months; Qatar's Ras Laffan facility—the world's largest LNG complex—sustained extensive damage from an Iranian missile strike in March with repairs estimated at up to five years. European storage sits at just 38%, well below the five-year seasonal average of over 50%, raising alarm over winter refill capacity. TTF eased back to ~€47.7/MWh on Tuesday as Trump signalled ongoing talks.

news.headline: Cocoa Surges ~10% on Ivory Coast Flooding; El Niño 'Super Event' Risk at 67%
news.body: ICE NY and London cocoa futures each jumped roughly 10% on Tuesday to 1.5-week highs, driven by heavy rains in Ivory Coast that caused flooding in key growing regions and cut off farmer access to plantations. NOAA estimates an 82% probability that El Niño conditions will emerge between May and July and persist through year-end, with a 67% chance of a 'Super El Niño' that could damage the West African crop. The Strait of Hormuz closure compounds the pressure by restricting fertiliser supply flows and pushing up shipping costs for cocoa importers. StoneX had already cut its 2026/27 global cocoa surplus estimate to 149,000 MT from 267,000 MT in late April, citing El Niño crop risks.
